sanskrit_verse:
भर्त्रा पित्रा सुतैर न स्त्री वियुक्तान्यगृहे वसेत् ।
असत्सङ्गे विशेषेण गर्ह्यतामेति सा ध्रुवम् ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration: bhartrā pitrā sutair na strī viyuktānyagṛhe vaset | asatsaṅge viśeṣeṇa garhyatāmeti sā dhruvam || 9 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: A woman shall not dwell in any house separated from her husband, father, or sons; dwelling in bad company brings inevitable reproach upon her.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through relational dharmic alignment, not individual autonomy
Causation arises from dislocation from rightful relational support
Capacity-based responsibility is context-dependent and relationally anchored
Restoration logic requires reintegration into dharmically aligned structures
Consciousness alignment depends on proximity to sattvic relational environments
executable_legal_axioms: IF a woman resides without husband, father, or sons, THEN system MUST initiate relational integrity assessment
IF residence occurs in unsuitable social environment, THEN automatic alert for consciousness-risk evaluation SHALL be triggered
IF reproach potential is detected, THEN restoration protocol MUST activate within 24 hours
NO punitive action SHALL occur; all interventions MUST preserve dignity and relational continuity
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that personal autonomy cannot override relational dharmic obligations. The threshold of responsibility lies not in moral fault but in structural misalignment. Courts must prioritize restoration of relational harmony over punitive measures, ensuring constitutional protection aligns with dharma-prescribed integration.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa shows that isolation from dharmic relational structures creates sequential manifestation of vulnerability and reproach. Responsibility is proportional to the degree of supported alignment. Non-punitive reality rule demands that corrective measures restore relational capacity rather than impose penalties.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Relational Reintegration Process: Assign guardian or family council to reestablish dharmic housing
Consciousness Environment Audit: Evaluate and redirect living conditions toward sattvic association
Completion Ritual: Formal acknowledgment and closure of reproach through community affirmation
Integrity Restoration Pathway: Legal facilitation of return to dharmically sound familial or societal structure
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. Dharma is restored through relational reintegration. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness stands as the ultimate adjudicator.
